Drift velocity: why the estimators disagree, and the starting-angle fix

MX17 bench re-run, 2026-10-24 · CHECKS C18/C19 · generated by rerun/seedfit/make_report.py

Verdict. det3 is consistent: the reconstruction's own drift velocity is 36.01 ± 0.13 (X) and 35.75 ± 0.15 (Y) µm/ns against the timing v of 35.8 ± 0.6. The calibration fit's free v is not a measurement (χ² flat along v). On det2/4/6/7 four measured effects stop the estimators closing: no dead-strip masks in any bench bundle (small), a scrambled channel order in det7 X connectors 0/1/3, a drift velocity that varies across det4/6/7, and an RC kernel that fits det4/det7 much worse than the old one. The starting-angle problem has an opt-in fix in wft.reco (WFT_PIVOT_START=1).

Three different "v"s

  • Timing v = gap / drift time. Gap from the charge extent of inclined tracks (no timing), T from head-on stacks. Kernel-free.
  • Reconstruction (ladder) v = slope of the fitted transverse speed w against the M3 angle. The per-event fit never uses v; the bundle's v × kw is only an angle scale.
  • Calibration fit with v free: χ² nearly flat along v, so its minimum is set by how the M3 reference pins the line. Not a measurement.

The starting-angle problem

At the right mesh position p0, χ² along w has one narrow well (3–5 µm/ns). But p0 is the mesh end of the track, up to w × (half the column) ≈ 5 mm from the charge, so a fit started at w = 0 on the brightest strip sits in a diagonal valley beside a broad w ≈ 0 shelf. Two more defects: the RC kernel's χ² is a 5 ns staircase in t0, and the ±5 ns t0 prior is invisible against χ² of 10⁴–10⁶.

Pivot start: a straight track passes through its own charge centroid (xc, tc), model-free (tc = charge-weighted sample time minus the impulse response's own time centroid, since convolution adds means). Scan w with the line forced through it and refine the two best wells.

Why det2/4/6/7 do not close

  1. No dead masks / gains in the bench bundles. Derived from the data (strip_health.py): masking moves the ladder ≤ 0.5 %; gains help det2/det4 X by 1–2 % but cost det3 resolution.
  2. det7 X connectors 0, 1, 3 are scrambled. True neighbours sit 5/10/15 channels apart; positions survive but angles are lost there.
  3. v varies over det4/6/7. X and Y ladder maps (independent readouts) agree, and the stacked drift time anti-correlates with them.
  4. RC kernel mismatch on det4/det7 (table above). det6's timing v assumed a 30 mm gap; ladder × T implies ≈ 27.5–28 mm, i.e. v ≈ 24, as the ladder reads.

What this does not rule out

  • The timing v carries 2–4 % (gap, stack-end definition); det6's gap is unmeasured and det7's long/longer runs differ by 12 %.
  • The kernel comparison uses the old bundles as delivered; which kernel is right on det4/det7 is judged by χ² only.
  • det7 X's channel scramble is identified but not mapped (≈150 events per connector); its pattern is not yet understood.
  • Regional v uses 3 × 3 regions with 60–280 events each; the per-region timing T comes from head-on tracks only.
  • All of this is the bench June data with RC it0 bundles; the pass will use final bundles.
